newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sends letter on anonymous accounts to Austria.
newsitem.headline: EU sends letter on anonymous accounts to Austria.

text.p: The European Commission will send a letter to the Austrian government on Wednesday setting out its position on Austria's anonymous savings accounts, a European Union official said on Tuesday.

The letter is being delivered as a result of a decision by the European Union executive last July to go a stage further in formal proceedings against Austria over a law which still allows people to hold anonymous accounts.
The letter has been signed by EU Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti, the official said.
Unless the Commission receives a satisfactory response to the so called "reasoned opinion" within two months, it could take Vienna to the European Court of Justice.
In July, the Commission said it was taking its action under an EU law aimed at stamping out laundering of money obtained through dubious means such as drugs trafficking.
Under the law there are obligations on banks to secure customer identification when a bank account is opened and for the bank to keep supporting evidence.

Austria formally outlawed anonymous securities accounts last August, a move welcomed by the EU executive. But the Commission said at the time it was unhappy about the continued existence of some 26 million anonymous savings books.
